A

Predii Learn — the “calibration” page

The historical processing is strong Predii core. The gap is legibility: someone being demoed to can’t see what all this learning is for, or feel the “aha” moment when the brain becomes theirs.

A1

Say what the knowledge is for

Quick win

Articulate on the Learn page what this processed knowledge actually drives downstream (canned jobs, pricing, recommendations). Today it reads as data-crunching with no payoff stated.

A2

Add a “calibration complete” moment

Quick win

When processing finishes, surface a clear personalization state — e.g. a pop-up / banner: “Predii LLM is now calibrated for your shop.” Make the link visible: this run → your shop-specific WrenchIQ brain.

A3

Tie insights to the engine

Core build

Repeat-customer, seasonal and canned-job/pricing insights are compelling — explicitly show they feed recommendations (“no need to look up parts/pricing, it’s from your own data”).

B

Shop setup — Strategic Priorities & tone

The free-text → rule pipeline for priorities is exactly right. Two refinements: separate standing from time-bound priorities, and add a tone-of-voice control.

B1

Split standing vs. time-bound priorities

Quick win

Margin / ARO / ELR are standing targets that don’t change. “This week, offer a brake-fluid flush” is time-bound. Present two buckets so ongoing targets aren’t mixed with tactical campaigns.

B2

Make the targets free-form

Core build

ARO/ELR/margin are the defaults, but let a shop swap in what they actually care about — e.g. technician productivity instead of ARO. Same LLM-rule pipeline, just not hard-coded.

B3

Add a tone-of-voice setup

Core build

Today the only guidance to the model is “don’t be salesy.” Let the shop pick a voice: professional vs. neighborhood-shop, concise vs. verbose, and whether to share evidence (“80% of customers like you did this”). A higher-end shop wants a different register.

C

Repair order — write-back, closed loop & scoring

Three of the highest-value asks came from the RO view: writing back to the SMS, closing the loop on recommendations, and scoring ROs on two independent axes.

C1

Read-only vs. read/write to the SMS

Core buildOpen question

Mitchell 1 is connected read-only. Offer a read/write tier where the SMS API allows it (Snap-on/Jake’s note: hand the transfer back to Mitchell 1). Natural pricing lever (+$10 to write back), plus a disclaimer that the shop owner owns the transfer.

C2

Close the loop on recommendations

Core build

Log every recommendation made, then track whether it was implemented — even if the advisor never clicks “Add to RO” (they may add it manually later). Detect it on RO refresh, show a check, and measure recommendation → conversion.

C3

Two RO scores, not one

Core build

Keep the Gold-Standard completeness/hygiene score (the “RO Score 40%”), but add a separate opportunity score — how much upsell juice is really in this RO/customer. Surface both on the queue and let advisors sort, so they spend time where it pays.

Sort by opportunity to find the upsell; sort by hygiene to find sloppy ROs.

D

Chat / Rewrite assistant

Rewrite is a real want (shops do this in ChatGPT today). Make it pull from the RO, add preset tasks, and consider exposing a public model — all inside WrenchIQ.

D1

Pull the concern from the RO

Quick win

Don’t make the advisor retype or paste the customer concern — it’s already in the RO. Since WrenchIQ has the RO, pre-fill it.

D2

Preset task buttons

Quick win

One-click actions: Rewrite concern, Rewrite CCC, Look up a price, Look up a symptom — like the old Service Writer Assist. Pre-build the most common tasks.

D3

Optional public-model toggle

Core buildOpen question

Shops already pay $20/mo for ChatGPT. Let them run those tasks inside WrenchIQ against a public model (ChatGPT/Claude) with a legal acknowledgment — and guardrails so certain queries stay Predii-only. Pricing: undercut their $20 (charge ~$10). Tokens are cheap.

D4

Research the real use cases

Open question

Ask the friendly shop owner for their top-5 ChatGPT use cases and pre-build them. The most valued items are usually simple.

Mock-up — preset tasks + model toggle
Predii LLMPublic (ChatGPT/Claude)
E

Owner / manager chat — outside the RO

Chat only lives inside an RO today. Owners don’t just use ChatGPT while inside an RO — add a chat entry point at the queue / dashboard level.

E1

Add a chat button at the queue level

Core build

Manager-type questions: “How’s my business today?”, “Which open ROs need my attention?” Runs on the current Predii model — no OpenAI needed. Big differentiator: no shop can query its own SMS data in ChatGPT/Claude today unless it built its own MCP server.

E2

Role-based access

Core build

Not every service writer should see all financials across every RO — gate owner/manager views by role.

F

Trim the SMS surface — less is more

F1

Hide non-core features from the SMS view

Quick win

The representative SMS view should be Kanban + auto queue, full stop. Move/hide extras like the 3C Story Writer — they pull attention from the core. (Agreed live: “Less is more.”)

F2

Fix the missing Home button

Quick win

Minor nav gap noted during the demo — no home button to get back to the queue.

G

The hub vision — beyond a 1:1 with the SMS

Push the thinking: WrenchIQ shouldn’t be a one-to-one pipe between the SMS and the overlay. Where does RO / business info need to go next, what is it combined with, and what actions should it trigger?

G1

Connect the other systems the shop runs

V2 / Vision

Accounting (QuickBooks), email (Outlook/Gmail), comms (Teams/Slack), calendar. Taylor’s point: WrenchIQ is powerful precisely because it can sit on top of more than the SMS.

G2

Trigger cross-system actions

V2 / Vision

“Send Nathan a Slack about X,” “drop a calendar invite for Tuesday to review Y,” “build the next team-meeting agenda into the Google Sheet.” Useful for multi-location shops where managers coordinate.

G3

Frame the hub questions

V2 / Vision

For each piece of info (SMS, RO, business performance): where does it flow, what does it combine with, what actions must it trigger, and how does WrenchIQ embed in that? Fringe for now — don’t let it distract from the core — but it’s the direction.
